item.title: Pond and Parishwood empty of water revealing dumped objects, 12th August
item.description:
Due to the ongoing drought, the water levels at Parish Wood pond has significantly dropped showing the various objects thrown in the pond since last year. These include am office chair, a bike and unfortunately a glass fish tank that has smashed into small pieces. Additionally, there are large branches, empty bottles, footballs etc. I am concerned that the glass will remain in the pond and injure the ducks and geese when they return to the pond once it fills up again. Also local children are now playing in the mud at the bottom of the pond. Is it possible for a team to collect the discarded objects so that the pond is in a better state when the rains fill the pond back up in the autumn? It makes sense to do this whilst the pond is empty. Myself, and local residents, would be more than happy to clear this area ourselves if the council could the rubbish away for us or provide a skip. Thank you.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Parish Gate Drive, Falconwood, Greater London

item.title: We recently reported that the build-up of dry leaves in the alleyway was creating a significant fire hazard, particularly due to smokers discarding cigarette butts in the area. We subsequently received an update confirming that action had been taken.Unfortunately, although your contractors attended, they only cleared a few metres of the alleyway before stopping and leaving. The work was therefore not completed as stated, and the majority of the leaves remain. Given the current dry conditions and the ongoing risk of discarded cigarette butts causing a fire, could you please arrange for the area to be properly cleared as soon as possible?We would appreciate this being followed up and completed in full, rather than leaving the work partially finished., 12th August
